solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pirate's underwear turned vile with runs

parts.note: long johns are long woollen underpants

indicators.note: turned says the letters of vile, with the extra letter, are twisted into a new order

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A buccaneer's underclothes have gone foul after a bout of diarrhoea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' rearranges VILE plus R into ILVER. The 's on Pirate's reads as 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The one-legged buccaneer of Stevenson's Treasure Island, so a famous example of a pirate.

clue.text: Excess fluid covers pillow somewhat

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Spilt liquid soaks through to the bedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid that floods beyond its container is the surplus, an example of excess fluid.

clue.text: Eagle coming up following golf class

indicators.note: following places the eagle after the golf letter

parts.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: an erne is a sea eagle

explanation.surface: A bird of prey appears after a lesson on the golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'coming up' reads the bird backwards, upwards from the bottom of the light.
explanation.definitionFit: A genre is a category or kind of art, so a synonym for class.

clue.text: Not working close is displeasing

parts.note: a machine that is off is not working
the close of a story is its ending

explanation.surface: A closing time for idleness is unwelcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Something offending causes annoyance or displeasure, a synonym for displeasing.

clue.text: Regularly sneer at rush approaches

indicators.note: regularly says take every other letter of the following words

explanation.surface: Someone habitually scoffs at haste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes the 2nd, 4th, 6th letters and so on of SNEER AT RUSH.
explanation.definitionFit: To near something is to come close to it, so nears is a synonym of approaches.

clue.text: Explain playwright dropping intro? About time

indicators.note: the opening letter of the playwright's name is dropped down to the end of the word

parts.note: Harold Pinter was a British playwright
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A puzzled theatregoer asks a dramatist to cut the introduction, saying it's about time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping intro' means the playwright's first letter is not lost but drops to the end of his name.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpret something is to make its meaning clear, so it is a synonym for explain.

clue.text: Content to forgive misspelled sign

indicators.note: misspelled says those inner letters are written in the wrong order
content means the inside of the next word, without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone is happy to pardon a sign written with a spelling mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content to' takes ORGIV from FORGIVE and 'misspelled' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgo, the Virgin, is one of the twelve zodiac signs, so an example of a sign.

clue.text: Value soldiers quietly infiltrating group

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

indicators.note: infiltrating means getting inside, so the quiet letter goes into the group

parts.note: a sect is a group with shared beliefs
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Troops creep silently into a band of followers.
explanation.definitionFit: To respect someone is to hold them in esteem, so a verb synonym for value.

clue.text: Scandi Noir, not one policeman cold?

indicators.note: not one says the one letter is taken out of the word noir

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
DI is a detective inspector
C is cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian crime drama with no detective out in the chill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes I from NOIR, leaving NOR. Scandi noir is the genre of Nordic crime fiction, so the surface stays in scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Scandi is informal for Scandinavian, which Nordic broadly means as an adjective.

clue.text: The drink hock; seal and all wrapping removed

indicators.note: each of the three words loses its outer letters, its wrapping, keeping only its middle

explanation.surface: Someone unwraps a bottle of German white wine, removing the seal and all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all wrapping removed' leaves OC, EA and N from HOCK, SEAL and AND. Hock is a German white wine, but here it is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The drink is slang for the sea, so a fitting name for the ocean.

clue.text: French ones crossing channel to bring back chips

indicators.note: crossing says the ones span the channel, holding it inside

parts.note: an ace is the one in a suit of cards

indicators.note: bring back says the channel's word is read in reverse

parts.note: a rut is a groove or channel

explanation.surface: French people crossing the Channel return with chips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bring back' reverses the channel word before 'crossing' puts it inside the ones. Chips here is a verb, not fried potatoes.
explanation.definitionFit: To chip a bone or a plate is to crack it, so fractures and chips are synonymous verbs.

clue.text: Pick out record, Queen number

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
ER is Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A DJ picks a record by the band Queen with a number on it.
explanation.definitionFit: To discern something is to make it out or perceive it, a synonym of pick out.

clue.text: One tight score revised, letting in own goal

indicators.note: letting in places the own goal inside the reworked score
revised means the letters of score are put in a new order

parts.note: OG is the football abbreviation for own goal

explanation.surface: A close match ends with the score changed after a team concedes an own goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' rearranges the score into SCROE before 'letting in' adds the goal. Tight means miserly, not close.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's Ebenezer is the archetype of a miser, someone tight with money.

clue.text: Gent nabbed by policeman turned terse

indicators.note: turned says the whole assembly is read backwards
nabbed by means held inside the policeman's letters

parts.note: PC is a police constable
sir is a polite form of address for a gentleman

explanation.surface: A gentleman arrested by a constable becomes short-tempered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nabbed by' gives PSIRC, and 'turned' reverses the whole of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisp reply is brief and to the point, a synonym of terse.

clue.text: Climbing plant starts to hatch, passer-by marvels

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the letters are read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: an anemone is a flowering plant

indicators.note: starts to takes the opening letters of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A climbing plant begins to sprout and a passer-by is amazed.
explanation.walkthrough: ANEMONE plus H and P is ANEMONEHP; 'Climbing' turns it upwards. 'Climbing plant' looks like one idea but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenomena are remarkable things or people, so wonders or marvels.

clue.text: International partners joining desperate rebel

parts.note: N and S, North and South, are partners in bridge
an urgent need is a desperate one

explanation.surface: A global alliance teams up with a frantic rebel.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurgent is one who rises in revolt against authority, a synonym for rebel.

clue.text: Material repairing hips and knees

indicators.note: repairing means the letters of hips and knees are put back together in a new order

explanation.surface: A surgeon uses some material to fix hips and knees.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheepskin is leather with the fleece left on, an example of material.

clue.text: Come across military officer uniform within lodge

indicators.note: within places the officer and the letter inside the word for lodge

parts.note: to lodge a complaint is to enter it
an NCO is a non-commissioned officer
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Meet a uniformed officer inside a masonic lodge.
explanation.definitionFit: To encounter someone is to meet them unexpectedly, a synonym of come across.

clue.text: Mate's dog shaking current fever

indicators.note: shaking off, the current's letter is shed from the dog

parts.note: a collie is a sheepdog
I is the physics symbol for electric current
ague is an old word for a malarial fever

explanation.surface: A friend's dog is trembling with an electric current and a fever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaking' removes I from COLLIE, leaving COLLE. The 's on Mate's reads as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A colleague is a workmate, so a fair synonym for a mate on the job.

clue.text: Love to interrupt uncle's bad advice

indicators.note: to interrupt means the love letter breaks into the reworked word
bad says those letters come out in the wrong order

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, leaving the letters UNCLES
O is love, a nil score in tennis

explanation.surface: A loving relative interrupts an uncle's poor advice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges UNCLES into CUNSEL, and 'to interrupt' puts O after its C.
explanation.definitionFit: Counsel is guidance given to someone, a synonym of advice.

clue.text: Vulgar eccentric having head in textbook for week

indicators.note: for says the head letter takes the place of the week's letter

parts.note: wacky means odd or eccentric

indicators.note: head in takes the first letter of the word textbook

explanation.surface: An oddball has their head stuck in a textbook all week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head in' gives T and 'for' swaps it in for the W of WACKY.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacky means cheap and in poor taste, a synonym of vulgar.

clue.text: Finally, enemy and old ruler uniting

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of enemy

parts.note: a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: At last foe and ancient monarch come together.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoking means joining as if under a yoke, a synonym of uniting.

clue.text: Removes jam from one in French footwear

parts.note: un is French for one
clogs are wooden shoes

explanation.surface: Someone in French wooden shoes clears a blockage.
explanation.definitionFit: To unclog a pipe is to clear what blocks it, so freeing a jam.

clue.text: 150 train for profession

parts.note: CL is 150 in Roman numerals
to train a gun is to aim it

explanation.surface: A hundred and fifty people train for a career.
explanation.walkthrough: Profession here is a declaring, as in a profession of faith, not a career.
explanation.definitionFit: A profession is an avowal or assertion, so a synonym of claim in that sense.

clue.text: Boat from south on circular course

parts.note: a loop is a circuit or circular course

explanation.surface: A vessel heads south on a round trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A sloop is a single-masted sailing vessel, an example of a boat.

clue.text: Draw over books, whatever's available

indicators.note: over says the draw word covers or goes over the books, holding them inside

parts.note: to pluck is to pull or draw out
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A lottery draw over some books makes do with whatever comes.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking potluck means accepting what turns up, so it describes whatever's available.

clue.text: I live in dry mountainous region

indicators.note: in places the two pieces inside the letters for dry

parts.note: TT is teetotal, meaning dry or not drinking
to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: Someone says they live in an arid highland area.
explanation.definitionFit: Tibet is the Himalayan plateau, an example of a mountainous region.

clue.text: Electrician restricting moisture, ordinary toil

indicators.note: restricting means the electrician's word confines the other letters inside it

parts.note: spark or sparks is slang for an electrician
dew is moisture condensed overnight

explanation.surface: An electrician keeping out damp has an everyday job.
explanation.definitionFit: Spadework is the hard groundwork for a task, a synonym of toil.

clue.text: Staff flap about working

indicators.note: about says the word for flap turns around

parts.note: a tab is a small flap of material
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: Employees fuss about work.
explanation.walkthrough: Staff here is a stick, not employees.
explanation.definitionFit: A baton is a short stick or rod, a sense of staff.

clue.text: Spinal Tap played up current album

indicators.note: played means the letters of up current album are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: The rock band Spinal Tap played an album louder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinal Tap' looks like the spoof rock band, which suits 'played' and 'album'; here it is the American medical term.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinal tap is the American name for drawing fluid from the lower spine with a needle.
